entries.title: Vikings lose wide receiver Justin Jefferson in 23-16 win over Buccaneers
entries.summary: <p>TAMPA, Fla. — Myles Price returned a punt 86 yards for a score, Kyler Murray threw a 41-yard TD pass to Jordan Addison and the Minnesota Vikings beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 23-16 on Sunday.</p><p>It was a costly game for both teams.</p><p>Baker Mayfield hurt his thumb on a desperation pass late in the fourth quarter. He was screaming in pain on the ground before walking off and was replaced by rookie Jalon Daniels in the final minute.</p><p>Two-time All-Pro wide receiver Justin Jefferson didn't return for Minnesota after injuring his right ankle in the first quarter.</p><p>The Vikings are 3-0 for the second time in three years. The Buccaneers are 0-3 for the first time since 2014, when they finished 2-14 and got the No. 1 overall draft pick, taking Jameis Winston.</p><p>Murray was 15 of 29 for 168 yards with one TD pass and one interception in his first full game with the Vikings. He sustained a concussion in the first quarter of the season opener and Carson Wentz led Minnesota to consecutive wins.</p><p>Mayfield hasn't played like a $55 million-a-year quarterback since the Buccaneers gave him a $165 million extension before the season. He was 17 of 34 for 217 yards with one TD and one interception, taking six sacks.</p><p>Tampa Bay's woeful offense couldn't do much against coordinator Brian Flores' defense.</p><p>Mayfield had an 85-yard touchdown pass to Chris Godwin Jr. on third-and-30 negated by a holding penalty on Luke Goedeke in the third quarter.</p><p>That summed up the offense's struggles.</p><p>Mayfield's 14-yard scramble on second-and-9 later was negated by a holding penalty on Payne Durham. But the Bucs got a first down on third-and-29 when Joshua Metellus hit Emeka Egbuka helmet-to-helmet. Again, the offense had to settle for a field goal. Chase McLauglin's 54-yarder cut it to 17-16.</p><p>Will Reichard's 56-yard field goal extended Minnesota's lead to 20-16 with 3:10 remaining. He added a 43-yarder to cap the scoring.</p><p>Murray connected with Addison on a deep throw on third-and-8 to give the Vikings a 17-10 lead in the second quarter. Addison beat Jacob Parrish in one-on-one coverage, making a smooth adjustment on the ball.</p><p>After A'Shawn Robinson intercepted Murray's pass to set up a first down at the Vikings 22 in the third quarter, the Bucs went nowhere. Bucky Irving ran 3 yards and then dropped a pass. Mayfield got sacked on third down and McLaughlin's 38-yarder cut it to 17-13.</p><p>The Buccaneers fell behind 10-0 after just one possession. Following a three-and-out, Price darted up the middle, cut to the right and sprinted down the sideline for his first career touchdown.</p><p>Mayfield fired a 40-yard TD pass down the seam to rookie Ted Hurst III to cut it to 10-7.</p><p>The Buccaneers had a first down at Minnesota's 7 after Mayfield and Cade Otton connected on a 37-yard pass. But consecutive holding penalties on Cody Mauch and Graham Barton derailed the drive and McLaughlin kicked a 28-yard field goal to tie it.</p><h3>Brotherly love</h3><p>Buccaneers left guard Ben Bredeson played against his younger brother, Vikings rookie fullback Max Bredeson. Their older brother, Jack, is the director of player information for the New York Mets. All three went to Michigan.</p><h3>Injuries</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Vikings:</b> Jefferson injured his right ankle when a defender fell on it. He walked to the locker room after watching a couple series. ... P Brett Thorson (hamstring) was inactive. ... CB Charles Demmings left with a hamstring injury.</p><p><b>Buccaneers:</b> Edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. (groin) and LB Josiah Trotter (shoulder) were inactive. ... WR Jalen McMillan left in the first quarter with a knee injury and didn't return.</p><h3>Up next</h3><h3></h3><p><b>Vikings:</b> Host Miami next Sunday.</p><p><b>Buccaneers:</b> Host Green Bay next Sunday.<br></p>

entries.title: Lyons' EJ Kuhlman is on a roll
entries.summary: <p>Playing high school football and baseball keeps Lyons senior EJ Kuhlman pretty busy.</p><p>But what does he do in his downtime?</p><p>“I love playing pickleball with my friends,” Kuhlman told the Sun-Times. “I think that’s actually got me on my toes.”</p><p>There’s no doubt the 5-9, 177-pound Kuhlman’s footwork is elite.</p><p>He’s in his second season as the lead running back for the Lions (5-1, 2-1 West Suburban Silver), who have clinched their sixth consecutive IHSA playoff berth.</p><p>Last year against York in the regular season, Kuhlman ran 43 times for a program-record 246 yards. Some other records could be in play this season, but he’s not interested in talking about them.</p><p>“My main goal is just winning conference first,” he said. “I don’t really care about the stuff that comes with it.</p><p>“I mean, it’s awesome to get those records at the end of the season, see what you’ve achieved. But you can’t really put all that credit on yourself . . . because you know a lot of that comes from coaches and O-linemen.”</p><p>He had 1,104 rushing yards and 15 touchdowns last fall and has scored at least one touchdown in every game this season with multiple 100-yard rushing games.</p><p>It’s a culmination of everything Kuhlman has been working toward.</p><p>“I always played flag football growing up, but I didn’t start tackle until seventh grade,” he said. “I was with the LFC [Lyons Football Club] program, and it was with a lot of my same buddies I play with now.”</p><p>Like most kids, Kuhlman tried a variety of sports growing up: soccer, basketball, tennis and wrestling in addition to the ones he’s still doing.</p><p>“You kind of play whatever your parents put you in,” he said. “Sports has always been part of my life, and it’s a big part of me and who I am.”</p><p>Until last year, Kuhlman didn’t really favor one sport over the other.</p><p>“Honestly, I was always split between baseball and football,” he said. “But junior year, I think I took football a lot more serious. I think I started to appreciate it a lot more. The amount of effort that goes into football is kind of what took me to love football more than baseball.</p><p>“But I still love both sports, very close to equal. But football is just a little different for me.”</p><p>That meant an extra level of preparation for his final high school season, focusing primarily on getting faster.</p><p>“Speed’s the biggest factor with a running back,” he said. “So you drop a couple of pounds to gain that extra point-one or point-two on that 40 [yard dash time].</p><p>“But I think this year, my goal is just to try not to get down — always break that first guy.”</p><p>The season of experience has paid off in other ways.</p><p>“What [is] different this year is kind of [being] comfortable,” Kuhlman said. “And I feel like [it’s been] to slow the game down and just realize that you kind of control it.”</p>
